recovery_pathway: Remove SIM card and memory card before handing in
Take the device to an authorised e-waste collection facility
Facility will safely extract the battery for licensed lithium recycling
PCB and display will be separated by certified recyclers for precious-metal recovery
Rare-earth magnets in speaker and motor recovered through industrial processes
safe_handling: Do not attempt to remove or puncture the battery yourself — risk of fire or chemical burn
Do not crush, burn, or incinerate the device
If the battery is swollen or damaged, place in a fireproof container and deliver to a certified collection point immediately
Handle cracked screens carefully to avoid glass cuts
Use only authorised e-waste recycling facilities for disposal
smartphones.reasoning_basis: Smartphones contain concentrated high-value materials (precious metals, rare earths) in a compact form factor, making per-unit recovery economically viable when processed by certified recyclers.

recovery_pathway: Back up and securely erase personal data from storage media before recycling
Deliver the complete laptop to a certified e-waste recycler
Certified facility will safely remove the battery for lithium recycling
Motherboard, RAM, and connectors processed for precious-metal recovery
Aluminium chassis and copper heat pipes recovered through industrial metal recycling
safe_handling: Do not attempt to remove the battery yourself — fire and chemical hazard
Do not burn or incinerate any laptop components
Wipe all personal data from storage before handing the device to a recycler
Older laptops may contain mercury in display backlights — handle as hazardous and leave disassembly to professionals
Use only certified e-waste recycling facilities for disposal
laptops.reasoning_basis: Laptops offer high material recovery value due to large PCBs, copper heat-pipe assemblies, and aluminium chassis, but require professional handling for battery and data-bearing components.

recovery_pathway: Collect and bundle cables for drop-off at a certified e-waste or scrap-metal facility
Facility will sort cables by conductor type (copper vs. aluminium)
Industrial cable-stripping machines will separate insulation from metal
Recovered copper and aluminium sent for smelting and reuse
PVC and rubber insulation handled by specialist plastic recyclers
safe_handling: Ensure cables are unplugged and fully de-energised before handling
Do not burn cables to remove their outer covering — PVC releases toxic fumes
Older cables may contain lead-stabilised PVC — leave processing to certified facilities
Use authorised e-waste or scrap-metal collection points for disposal
electrical_cables.reasoning_basis: Cables are high-volume, low-complexity e-waste with excellent copper recovery rates (>95%) through industrial mechanical stripping, making them one of the most cost-effective items to recycle.

recovery_pathway: Collect loose chips and circuit boards in anti-static packaging
Deliver to a certified e-waste recycler that handles electronic components
Certified smelters will extract gold, palladium, and copper through controlled processes
Ceramic-packaged chips routed to specialised ceramic-metal separation
safe_handling: Do not burn or incinerate chips — releases toxic brominated flame retardants and heavy metals
Do not attempt to extract metals yourself — requires industrial smelting
Older chips may contain hazardous beryllium oxide substrates — leave handling to professionals
Store in anti-static bags during collection and transport
Use only certified e-waste recycling facilities for disposal
electronic_chips.reasoning_basis: Individual chips are small but contain high-purity gold bond wires and palladium contacts; batch processing through certified smelters achieves economically viable precious-metal recovery.

recovery_pathway: Unplug the appliance and ensure it is fully powered off
Deliver the complete appliance to an authorised e-waste collection centre
Facility will safely remove batteries and capacitors
Metal housing, motors, and wiring recovered through industrial shredding and separation
PCBs routed to electronic component recycling for precious-metal recovery
safe_handling: Do not attempt to disassemble appliances yourself — capacitors may retain dangerous charge
Do not remove batteries yourself — take the complete unit to a certified facility
Do not burn or incinerate any appliance components
Very old appliances may contain hazardous materials (e.g. asbestos) — leave inspection to professionals
Use only authorised e-waste recycling or collection facilities for disposal
small_appliances.reasoning_basis: Small appliances are bulky but material-diverse; the primary recovery value comes from copper motor windings and steel housing, with PCBs providing supplementary precious-metal yield when processed by certified recyclers.
